name: BF-02 process fact register
source: BF-02 process fact register v1.1 (Claude Docs, 16 Oct 2026); machine copy for the Burden & Fuel Optimiser

grades.A: BF-02 trial or clean step change
grades.B: BF-02 regression or event study with a standard error

revision_log.change: STRATA 1.2 (rename of the gas-flow / shaft-efficiency model, formerly OMEGA): groups MOD (coke responses of Fixed-omega and STRATA-omega, generated by utils.burden_engine.model_facts) and VAL (out-of-sample burnt coke by blend family) added; GAS-13, 14, 15, 16, 18, 20, ASM-01, ASM-18 updated (RI set S8, production channel split, Investigate tier); GAS-21 (RI assumptions), GAS-22 (production against efficiency), DATA-12 (heat-loss coverage) added; statuses Modelled only and Neutral added.

OMEGA v1.1 after the out-of-sample test: GAS-14, GAS-15 replaced (per-group scales, AR(1) posterior on daily changes); GAS-17 retired (gas-capacity channel); GAS-19 (blast moisture), GAS-20 (out-of-sample test), FLOW-15, FLOW-16 (within-period resistance and stave heat load by material), DATA-11 (weather-record blast moisture) added; GAS-13, ASM-18, DATA-04, FLOW-02 notes updated.
Blend-dependent shaft efficiency (#262): GAS-13..18, ASM-18, ASM-19 added; GAS-06 and GAS-10 notes updated. No existing value changed.
Machine copy shipped with the Burden & Fuel Optimiser (#251). BAND-01: lower end implemented as a validity check, not an optimisation row (fact v1.1). No fact value changed.

Engine 2.0: RAFT from the plant workbook at the input blast moisture (DATA-03/04); BAND-01..03 enforced in code; webapp hand coefficients removed (COKE-17); COKE-14 no longer reports the ideal shaft. No fact value changed.
Register created: 17 COKE, 11 GAS, 14 FLOW, 10 DATA, 3 BAND and 13 ASM facts. Retired COKE-17 and DATA-10.

facts.statement: STRATA-omega: shaft efficiency from STRATA-Flow (BF-02 gas-flow model), ring counter-current reduction of wustite in the thermal reserve zone
facts.basis: BF-02 layered gas-flow model v0.4 (burden profile from the charging matrix, layered Ergun resistance, floating cohesive zone); six rings, eps-NTU with NTU = kappa k t_TRZ C_s / C_min; k from ISO 7215 RI and as-charged Sauter size, (11.25/d)^1.5; kappa fitted to the calibrated omega; quadratic surrogate (520-state DOE, CV omega RMSE 0.0002)
facts.literature: Rist & Meysson W-point shaft efficiency; counter-current exchanger analogy for gas-solid reduction
facts.note: STRATA 1.2 (formerly OMEGA). RI set S8 (GAS-21); kappa refitted at startup. Physics responses at the reference (per 10 wet pt): pellet for sinter +0.013, Lloyds CLO / Geomin for sinter -0.005, NMDC ROM for sinter -0.010, Gomti for sinter -0.005, oversize for sinter +0.004 (omega). The blend effect is kinetic (RI and size); the blend moves the radial gas shares by less than 0.002. Coke responses of both models: MOD-01..10.

facts.statement: Plant-data scales on the model channels of shaft efficiency (STRATA 1.2)
facts.basis: AR(1) Bayesian posterior of the daily change of omega against its 14-day anchor (191 days, 15 Dec 2025 - 7 Oct 2026, weather-record blast moisture), RI set S8: lam_pellet 1.27 +/- 0.43, lam_lump (Lloyds CLO, Geomin, NMDC ROM, Donimalai, Gomti, oversize) 0.47 +/- 0.35, production channel 0.68 +/- 0.29, other operating channel 1.37 +/- 0.28 (correlation +0.27); priors N(1, 0.5^2); rho 0.76. Selected out of sample (GAS-20).
facts.note: STRATA 1.1 used one operating scale (1.05 +/- 0.26) for production and the other operation; it over-predicted the production penalty (GAS-22). The lump-ore scale below 1 holds for every RI set tested (GAS-21): the data do not show the full kinetic penalty of lump ore at the physics size.

facts.statement: Pellet +10 wet pt -> shaft efficiency (STRATA 1.2, reference operation)
facts.basis: GAS-13 x GAS-14: pellet replacing sinter +0.0151 +/- 0.0054; replacing Lloyds CLO +0.0199 +/- 0.0059. 1 Jun 2026 pellet start (0 -> 14.5 %, Lloyds CLO -12 pt), 7 days either side: observed +0.080, moisture term +0.057 +/- 0.006 (13.4 g/Nm3), operation +0.002, remainder +0.021 +/- 0.022 against the v1.1 blend term +0.029 (14-day windows: remainder -0.002 +/- 0.028). The event is consistent with the model and does not narrow it.
facts.literature: Gas utilisation rises with pellet share (Indian pellets); supersedes the data-only estimate in GAS-06
facts.note: Coke response of both models at the reference point: MOD-01 (pellet for sinter) and MOD-08 (pellet for Lloyds CLO). Pellet above 25 % of ferrous is in the Investigate tier (GAS-18).

facts.statement: Production +1 t/h -> shaft efficiency (TRZ residence; STRATA 1.2 production channel)
facts.basis: Model (GAS-13) -0.0023 omega per t/h at the reference x plant-data scale 0.68 +/- 0.29 (GAS-14) = -0.0016 +/- 0.0007; data within months -0.0011 +/- 0.0008 (controls), -0.0018 +/- 0.0010 (month effects)
facts.literature: Shaft efficiency falls at high productivity (shorter residence)
facts.note: Coke: MOD-09 (Fixed-omega -0.38, STRATA-omega +0.04 kg/tHM per t/h at the reference). Data proof of the trade-off: GAS-22.

facts.statement: Gas quantity -> shaft efficiency (capacity ratio R = O_max,TRZ / (Y_W n_Fe), moved by its carbon-gas part)
facts.basis: Model (GAS-13) at R 0.70, NTU about 3; solved inside the two-zone balance (rist.solve_2z omega_fn). R follows the carbon gas only: H2 reduces wustite several times faster than CO and the ring model has no gas-side rate, so H2 is not counted as extra capacity (the data show omega rising with blast moisture, +0.0035 +/- 0.0011 per g/Nm3). Amplifies coke responses by about 1.35 (dK/domega -342 against -254 kg/tHM at fixed omega): HMT +10 degC 0.94 -> 1.26, Si +0.1 % 2.0 -> 2.7 kg/tHM
facts.note: Retired 21 Oct 2026 (OMEGA v1.1): out of sample the gas-capacity channel added no skill and its data scale was negative (expanding fits -0.5 to +0.2; -2.4 +/- 0.8 against the observed change, driven by moisture and Si). R is held at the calibration (omega_model.json gas_capacity_channel false).

facts.statement: Certainty tiers of a plan (STRATA-omega): High, Medium, Low, Investigate
facts.basis: High: sigma(coke) <= 2 kg/tHM and blend classes and production inside the 1st-99th percentile of the 200 days BF-02 ran; Medium: sigma <= 5 and within 5 pt / 3 t/h of that range; Low otherwise; Investigate: pellet above 25 % of ferrous or sigma(coke) above 8 kg/tHM (beyond common practice; 20 % pellet is standard, BF-02 ran <= 15 %). The default filter and auto mode exclude Investigate plans.
facts.note: User decision 22 Oct 2026 (Investigate at 25 % pellet). Low and Investigate results show their critical assumptions (RI, size exponent, plant-data scales) with the coke effect of each.

facts.statement: Blast moisture -> shaft efficiency (weather-record basis)
facts.basis: AR(1) posterior with GAS-14 (191 days); within months, excluding the record's monthly steps: 0.0051 +/- 0.0008. Equal to the arithmetic sensitivity of the calibrated omega to the assumed moisture (+0.0042 +/- 0.0006): the coke the balance adds for moisture (+0.8 kg/tHM per g/Nm3) is not seen in burnt coke (burnt minus model -1.2 +/- 0.2 per g/Nm3).
facts.literature: Hydrogen from blast moisture reduces wustite faster than CO; plant practice +1 g/Nm3 -> coke +0.6 to +1 kg/tHM
facts.note: Top-gas H2 shows no response to the record's day-to-day moisture (-0.001 +/- 0.005 % per g/Nm3; +0.04 - 0.05 expected). Whether the furnace's blast moisture follows the record day to day is therefore not established; the term keeps the coke prediction consistent with burnt coke either way. Net engine coke response -0.2 to -0.4 kg/tHM per g/Nm3.

facts.statement: Out-of-sample test of the shaft-efficiency model (STRATA 1.2)
facts.basis: Day minus its 14-day anchor, 175 days 1 Jan - 7 Oct 2026; parameters from earlier days only (monthly refit). Skill = 1 - MSE/MSE(Fixed-omega). STRATA 1.2: omega 0.256 (day); burnt coke 0.182 (day, RMSE 7.33 vs 8.11 kg/tHM), 0.188 (7-day). Time splits (train Dec-May / test Jun-Oct; reverse): burnt coke 0.233 / 0.166 (day). STRATA 1.1: 0.181 (day). OMEGA v1.0: -0.29. By blend family: VAL-01..12.
facts.note: The skill comes from the moisture term (about 0.11 in every sub-period), the operating channels and the pellet channel; within-period blend changes are 1 - 3 pt and carry little evidence. Families with fewer than 10 days (Gomti, ROM + oversize, pellet + oversize) are Modelled only. Data-only XGBoost: benchmark only.

facts.statement: Auto mode: the pick is a fixed rule; the language model only reviews it
facts.basis: Candidates: lowest expected cost, lowest cost + 1.28 sigma, High certainty only, today. Rule: lowest cost + 1 sigma among plans that meet every limit; keep today when the saving is below 1 sigma of the saving. Review: JSON, choice must be a candidate, numbers checked against the table, disagreement shown, never substituted

facts.statement: Reducibility (ISO 7215 RI) of pellet and lump ores used by STRATA-omega (set S8)
facts.basis: No plant RI test for pellet or lump ore. Sinter 68.7 % (plant mean, SP-02). S8: pellet 65, Lloyds CLO and oversize 65, NMDC ROM 65, Donimalai 60, Geomin and Gomti 75 %, from mineralogy (LOI: goethitic ores 5-8 % porous after dehydration, high RI; Bailadila hard hematite LOI < 2 %, dense, lower RI) and published ranges. Review of nine RI sets and size exponents on the 191 days: out-of-sample burnt-coke skill 0.178 - 0.182 for every RI set at n = 1.5 (0.195 - 0.204 at n = 1.0 / 0.5): the plant data cannot separate the RI sets.
facts.literature: ISO 7215; Indian hematite / goethite ores RI 55-80 % by LOI and porosity
facts.next_test: RI and RDI tests of NMDC ROM, Lloyds CLO, Gomti, Geomin and pellet (ISO 7215 / 4696)
facts.note: Proposal "NMDC ROM 65-75 %": adopted at 65 % (literature for dense Bailadila hematite does not support 70-75). Proposal "Gomti overstated": not supported - Gomti is goethitic (LOI 5-8 %), raised from 64 to 75 %. Proposal "Lloyds CLO understated": supported, 58 -> 65 %. Each result in the Low / Investigate tier shows the coke effect of RI +/- 5 pt per material; size exponent n is a second critical assumption.

facts.statement: Production against efficiency: dilution of the fixed heat loss against shorter TRZ residence (BF-02 data)
facts.basis: Within-month regressions (200 days, HAC): heat loss GJ/h per t/h -0.59 +/- 0.63 (fixed per hour: dilution 7.4 MJ/tHM per t/h); omega -0.0011 +/- 0.0008 per t/h; burnt coke -1.33 +/- 0.44, charged coke -0.89 +/- 0.51 kg/tHM per t/h. Out-of-sample residual against the production change: Fixed-omega -0.68 +/- 0.86, STRATA 1.1 -1.50 +/- 0.85, STRATA 1.2 -1.39 +/- 0.82 kg/tHM per t/h.
facts.literature: Higher productivity lowers fuel rate through heat-loss dilution until residence time limits gas use
facts.note: Dilution is confirmed; the residence penalty is about 0.6-0.7 of the physics (GAS-14). Net burnt coke falls with production in the record, partly through furnace condition (good days run faster): the coefficient is an upper bound on the benefit.

facts.statement: Measured cooling-water heat loss against the heat loss the balance needs
facts.basis: 568 shifts: cooling water flow x dT by circuit = 8.0 GJ/h (staves rows 6-10 5.0, hearth and bottom 2.7, tuyere noses 0.4) against 64 GJ/h required by the calibrated two-zone balance (692 MJ/tHM); coverage 13 % (10-18 % by month). Typical furnaces of this size report 50-70 GJ/h of wall and cooling loss.
facts.literature: Heat loss to cooling 0.5-0.8 GJ/tHM in comparable furnaces
facts.next_test: Verify flow meters; paired calibrated dT sensors per circuit; dT on rows 11-15 and the cold-surface circuits
facts.note: Rows 6-10 dT 1.1-2.4 K on 1,630 m3/h; tuyere nose dT 0.18 K (implausible); rows 11-15 and the rows 6-10 cold-surface circuits (657 m3/h design) have no dT measurement. The measured value cannot replace the calibrated loss (ASM-03); the gap is an instrumentation finding, not a heat-balance finding.
